questions.question: What defines an arithmetic sequence?
choices: A constant difference between consecutive terms
A constant ratio between consecutive terms

questions.question: What is the common difference in 5, 9, 13, 17, …?
What is the next term in 20, 17, 14, 11, …?
Which sequence is arithmetic?
What is the first term of the sequence given by aₙ = 3n + 2 for n = 1, 2, 3, …?
Which formula gives the nth term of an arithmetic sequence with first term a₁ and difference d?
Can an arithmetic sequence have a negative common difference?
choices: Only if all terms are negative
Yes; its terms decrease by a constant amount
Only if its first term is zero

questions.question: Why does the nth-term formula use n − 1 differences?
choices: The first term is never counted
There are n − 1 steps from the first term to the nth term
Every arithmetic sequence begins at index zero
The final difference must be omitted

questions.question: What is the tenth term of 7, 10, 13, …?
A sequence has first term 12 and difference −2. What is its sixth term?
Which recursive rule generates 4, 9, 14, 19, … after a₁ = 4?
An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 3 and a₄ = 18. What is its common difference?
How is an arithmetic sequence related to a linear function?
choices: Its values lie on a line at integer indices
Its values always lie on a circle
It has a constant percentage growth rate
It cannot be modeled with a formula

questions.question: Which formula generates 6, 10, 14, 18, … for n starting at 1?
A seating plan has 8 chairs in row 1 and 3 more chairs in each successive row. How many chairs are in row 7?
In 4, 9, 14, 19, …, which term is 49?
An arithmetic sequence has third term 11 and fifth term 19. What is its first term?
A sequence begins at 50 and decreases by 4. What is the first term below zero?
Two arithmetic sequences start at 2 and 20 and have differences 5 and 2 respectively. At which term index do their values first match?
A student says 3, 6, 12, 24 is arithmetic because each term increases. Which correction is valid?
choices: The sequence is arithmetic because all terms are even after the first
The differences vary; the sequence has a constant ratio instead
The sequence is constant because its rule does not change
